candidate.statement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to `k`. A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.

examples.explanation: Subarrays [1, 1] at indices [0, 1] and [1, 2] sum to 2.

hints: If the cumulative sum up to index j is S_j and up to index i-1 is S_{i-1}, the subarray sum from i to j is S_j - S_{i-1}.
If S_j - S_{i-1} == k, then S_{i-1} == S_j - k. Store prefix sum frequencies in a hash map.
short_diagnostics: Why must the prefix frequency map be initialized with {0: 1}?

evaluator.rubric: Learner must initialize prefix frequency map with base case {0: 1} and accumulate prefix_counts[cur_sum - k] before recording cur_sum.
known_pitfalls: Omitting {0: 1} base case in prefix counts, failing subarrays starting from index 0.
Assuming all numbers are positive and attempting two-pointer sliding window.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Because numbers can be negative, prefix sums may decrease, so monotonicity does not hold and sliding window fails.
